hypotheses.binder: (hupper : ∀ n x, x ∈ s.domain → ‖N n x‖ ≤ M)
hypotheses.justification: The upper bound on ‖N‖ (and the implicitly bound M, which occurs nowhere else in the statement) is used only to make the range of N precompact so that the abstract inversion lemmas of the library apply; the statement itself stays true without it. The only place the hypothesis enters is `CurlClassBounds.normalInverse_unweighted` → `PolynomialJets.inv` (CurlClassBounds.lean:917), where `compact_jet_bound` is applied to the compact set `Metric.closedBall 0 M ∩ {r | b ≤ |r|}` in order to bound the jets of r ↦ r⁻¹ on a compact set. That compactness device can be replaced: on the open set {r : ℝ | b/2 < |r|} the iterated derivatives of r ↦ r⁻¹ are explicit, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ k (fun r => r⁻¹) r‖ = k!/|r|^(k+1) ≤ k!·(2/b)^(k+1), so the uniform bound `C = m!·(2/b)^(m+1)` (already available up to order m) can be fed to Mathlib's `norm_iteratedFDerivWithin_comp_le` (Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/ContDiff/Bounds.lean, the very lemma used inside `PolynomialJets.compact_comp` at CurlClassBounds.lean:868), which requires only an open set and a bound on the outer function's jets, not compactness of the inner function's range. `hlower` guarantees the range of ‖N‖² lies in {r | b² ≤ r} ⊆ {r | b²/2 < |r|} and `hb : 0 < b` gives b² > 0, so the reciprocal (‖N‖²)⁻¹ is smooth there with jets bounded by a constant times (max jet bound of ‖N‖²)^m, i.e. still of the form C·scale^p; the rest of the proof (multiplication of classes in `pressureCoefficient_class`, then `band_smul` with `hfreq`) is unaffected by the removal, since `MemClass` algebra never uses boundedness of the normal. Degenerate cases are covered: the junk value (‖N‖²)⁻¹ = 0 at ‖N‖ = 0 cannot occur on s.domain because of `hlower`, and emptiness of s.domain only makes the conclusion vacuous. Note that `hb` and `hlower` cannot be dropped instead: for b = 0 (or with no lower bound at all) a jet-controlled family such as N n x = (x₁,0,0) has a simple zero, near which the jets of (‖N‖²)⁻¹ blow up, so the class conclusion fails; the three hypotheses hupper, hb, hlower are thus independent and only hupper is removable.
